prologue.text: I can't remember anything... not even my name.

prologue.name: Wan Mahora
prologue.text: Play a game of congkak with me. Win, and I'll help you remember.

memory1.text: Her husband is leaving... for war.
A travelling poet stays in the village. She is kind to him.
Whispers everywhere... they say she betrayed her husband.

memory2.text: Accused of adultery... and the chief wouldn't let her speak.
They tied her to that tree... to be put to death.
White... her blood was white. She was innocent.

reveal.name: Mahsuri
reveal.text: They said I betrayed my husband... with that poet.

reveal.name: Mahsuri
reveal.text: I told them I was innocent. They would not listen.

reveal.name: Mahsuri
reveal.text: If I had sinned, let my blood run red.

reveal.name: Mahsuri
reveal.text: But if I am innocent... let it run white.

reveal.name: Mahsuri
reveal.text: For this injustice, Langkawi will know no peace...

lines: Not long after, the Siamese came across the sea.
Elephants. Cannons. Soldiers on our shores.
curse.title: The Siamese invasion
body: Not long after Mahsuri died, a Siamese army crossed into Kedah and on to Langkawi.
Soldiers, cannons and war elephants came ashore. Villagers fled into the hills.

lines: They burned their own rice so the enemy could not take it.
curse.title: Padang Beras Terbakar
body: Rather than let the invaders take their food, the villagers burned their own rice stores.
The place is still called the Field of Burnt Rice. People say charred grains rise from the soil after heavy rain.

lines: The crops withered. The wells ran dry.
Langkawi was cursed... for what they did to me.
curse.title: Nothing would grow
body: After the war the land turned against them. Harvests failed, wells dried up and children went hungry.
The island stayed poor and forgotten, just as she had sworn.

lines: One by one, the families left.
Seven generations would pass before this island knew peace.
And I have waited here... all this time.
curse.title: Seven generations
body: Family after family left Langkawi. Whole villages stood empty.
Seven generations would pass before the island prospered again. And all that time, she waited.

dawn: The sun is rising... I can finally rest.
credits: The legend of Mahsuri binti Pandak Mayah
"L'armée siamoise en marche", Le Petit Journal, 1893 (public domain)
congkak is a traditional Malay seed game
Seven generations have passed. Rest now.

deadStare.name: Village Chief
deadStare.text: You should not have come back.

deadStare.name: Village Chief
deadStare.text: The court has already judged you.
